# /sw:help

Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`. Talk to the user in their language. Run nothing: this command only explains.

- **No argument:** show the list below to the user, translated into their language, keeping every command and its arguments exactly as written (in code). One section per group, one line per command: the command, then what it is for. Keep the marks "(you start it)", "(also by itself)" and "(local or staging only)" translated. Then end with four short lines: `<…>` is required and `[…]` optional; a command marked "also by itself" is also used by Claude when the task calls for it; they can ask in their own words instead of typing a command; `/sw:help <command>` explains one command in detail.
- **A command name** (with or without `/sw:`): read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and explain that command: what it is for, its arguments with one or two examples, what it needs first (the app running, the browser tools, a key in the environment, the user's answers), what it writes in `.quality/`, and what to do with the result. If the name is unknown, show the closest names from the list.

The audited app can be written in any language: the commands work on its pages and its files.

## Start and follow-up

- `/sw:from-zero` — The path from an idea to a launched web app or SaaS, in stages with a gate at the end of each (also by itself)
- `/sw:kickoff [notes about the project]` — Set up Shipwright in a new or existing project (you start it)
- `/sw:audit [full | quick | group | domain | criterion IDs | blockers] (empty = incremental)` — Run a scored quality audit of the current project across Shipwright's domains (or a subset), with evidence for every criterion (you start it)
- `/sw:fix [criterion IDs | blockers | number of issues]` — Fix the issues found by the latest Shipwright audit, by priority (blockers first), verifying each fix with the criterion's own check (you start it)
- `/sw:handoff [what to focus on]` — Write a short handoff file (.quality/handoff.md) so the next session resumes the current task without re-exploring the project (also by itself)
- `/sw:status` — Summary of the latest audit: scores, blockers, date (you start it)
- `/sw:report [--run R]` — Rewrites .quality/report.html: scores over time, screenshots of each step of the key tasks, review findings (you start it)
- `/sw:doctor` — Checks that Shipwright is really there for this project: marketplace known, sw@shipwright installed and enabled, modules, hooks, versions. Read only (you start it)
- `/sw:browser-setup` — Installs Playwright, axe-core and Chromium once, in the pack's cache (not in the project). Needed by the commands that open pages (you start it)
- `/sw:graph [refresh]` — Graphify status for this project (installed, fresh, recommended for its size), or a refresh of the code graph (you start it)
- `/sw:help [command]` — this list, or one command explained in detail

## Design

- `/sw:design [check | variants | screen name, flow ID or URL] (empty = the whole interface)` — Runs all the design work of the project in the right order with one command (you start it)
- `/sw:design-direction` — Turns the sites and apps a client likes into a visual direction and design tokens that can be checked (also by itself)
- `/sw:design-screens` — Designs how a screen is organised before it is coded (also by itself)
- `/sw:design-variants` — Raises the quality of a key screen or page by building several versions that really differ, measuring them, and having a blind jury compare them two by two before the user chooses, instead of producing one version and polishing it (also by itself)
- `/sw:design-review [flow-id | URL | screen name]` — Reviews an existing screen or key task and advises how to improve it, outside the scored audit (also by itself)
- `/sw:premium-craft` — Takes an interface from correct to cared-for, so that nothing gives it away as a quick or generated job (also by itself)
- `/sw:deslop-ui` — Makes a web or Tauri interface clean and not generic, and proves it by measuring the rendered page in a real browser (also by itself)
- `/sw:scroll-animation` — Builds scroll animations that work for everyone (also by itself)
- `/sw:look <url> [url...] [--mode persuade|operate|read] [--as account]` — Measures how a page looks: weighted generic "AI-made" signals, point of view, font sizes and families, radii, line length, small targets, reduced motion (you start it)
- `/sw:deslop <url> [--widths 375,768,1440] [--dark] [--as account]` — Measures spacing, alignment and execution of the rendered page, element by element, at several widths, with screenshots (you start it)
- `/sw:craft <url> [url...] [--mode persuade|operate|read] [--as account]` — Measures the finish of the rendered page: typography details, focus and hover states, controls the click reaches, transitions, images, icons, site icon, share image, 404 page (you start it)
- `/sw:stress <url> [--only slow,failing,long,narrow,dark,keyboard,no_script] [--as account]` — Finishing passes: the screen with a slow network, a failing server, texts three times longer, 320 px wide, dark theme, keyboard only, scripts off (you start it)
- `/sw:tokens [file.tokens.json...]` — Checks the design tokens: DTCG format, references, units, contrast in each theme, colours outside sRGB (you start it)
- `/sw:tiles [folder]` — Shows the style tiles (default .quality/design/tiles) side by side on a desktop and a phone, with the fonts each tile declares but does not load (you start it)
- `/sw:bank [site type]` — Reference bank: for a site type, what visitors expect, sites known to be excellent with the reason, what to avoid. Without a type, lists the types (you start it)
- `/sw:patterns [family | pattern | search <words>] [--type <site type>] [--surface persuade|operate|read|phone|desktop-app]` — Pattern bank: everything the pack can propose for an interface (navigation, motion, visual effects, features, page sections, UX laws, inspiration galleries, component libraries), with where each fits, what it costs and how to build it with free tools. Without an argument, lists the families (you start it)
- `/sw:profile <url> [url...] [--save]` — Measures the visual profile of pages in numbers (type scale, typefaces, first screen, colours, density). --save keeps them as the project's references (you start it)
- `/sw:gap <url> [--type <site-type>] [--device mobile]` — Compares a screen with the project's references, or with the reference bank of a site type (you start it)
- `/sw:variants <name> <url> <url> [url...] | <name> --tally` — Several versions of one screen: screenshots under shuffled letters, measures, pairs for a blind jury; --tally ranks them from the votes (you start it)

## Security

- `/sw:security-testing` — Tests the security of the user's own app for real instead of reading a checklist (also by itself)
- `/sw:access [--base URL] [--check]` — Plays access control for real: each declared resource is requested by its owner, then by the accounts that must not reach it. Exit code 2 when something leaks (you start it, local or staging only)
- `/sw:auth [--base URL]` — Tests the login: the right password first, same answer for known and unknown accounts, wrong passwords in a row slowed or refused. Also sign-up and password reset when declared (you start it, local or staging only)
- `/sw:dast [url] [--minutes N]` — Passive security scan of the running app with OWASP ZAP in Docker: headers, cookies, information leaks, vulnerable libraries (you start it, local or staging only)
- `/sw:supply` — Reads the supply chain of the repository: lockfile, delay before installing new versions, install scripts, pinned CI actions, .env files, commands that tool configuration runs by itself (you start it)
- `/sw:threats [--check | --gate launch]` — Checks the threat model (.quality/threats.json): every entry point covered, a response and a test for each abuse case (you start it)
- `/sw:webhooks [--base URL]` — Plays the webhooks: an unsigned or wrongly signed event must be refused (you start it, local or staging only)

## Speed, search and content

- `/sw:seo-launch` — Gets the public pages of a site found on search engines, from the choice of keywords to the launch (also by itself)
- `/sw:perf <url> [url...]` — Measures loading on a slowed-down phone: largest paint, layout shift, blocking time, weight of the page and of its scripts (you start it)
- `/sw:seo [url] [--limit N]` — Search readiness of the public pages: sitemap, title and meta description of each page, one h1, target keywords carried by their page, Search Console (you start it)
- `/sw:web <url>` — HTTP checks of a page: security headers, compression, cache, SEO metadata, robots, sitemap (you start it)
- `/sw:facts <url> [url...]` — Lists the figures, quotes, customer names and badges shown on public pages, and checks each one is traced in .quality/facts.json (you start it)
- `/sw:scan` — Static scans of the source: placeholders, hollow wording, debugging leftovers (you start it)

## SaaS and payments

- `/sw:saas-foundations` — Builds the parts every SaaS needs and that are costly to add late (also by itself)
- `/sw:billing [--wait seconds]` — Plays the subscription life cycle in Stripe's test mode with a test clock: trial, first payment, declined renewal, cancellation; the app is asked what it believes at each stage (you start it, local or staging only)

## Key tasks and real people

- `/sw:flows [task id...] [--base URL] [--attach port]` — Plays the key tasks declared in project.json on a phone and a desktop, step by step: screenshot, accessibility and effort at every step (you start it)
- `/sw:record <task id> [--start /path] [--device desktop|mobile]` — Records a key task while the user does it in a browser, and saves it as a flow in project.json (you start it)
- `/sw:user-testing` — Prepares, runs and reports a test of the product with five real people from its audience (also by itself)

## Mobile and desktop apps

- `/sw:mobile-app` — Builds and releases an installed mobile app (iOS, Android) next to a web app without the usual rejections (also by itself)
- `/sw:mobile flows [task id...] | audit | check` — Installed mobile app. flows: plays the key tasks with Maestro on an emulator or device. audit: reads the screen shown on Android (touch targets, controls without a name). check: reads in the project what blocks a store release (you start it)
- `/sw:desktop-app` — Builds and releases a desktop app made with web technology (Tauri, Electron) that behaves like a real desktop app and does not expose the user's machine (also by itself)
- `/sw:desktop check` — Desktop app (Tauri, Electron): reads in the project what blocks or weakens a release: content security policy, permissions, isolation, updater, signing. Key tasks in the real window: /sw:flows --attach <port> (you start it)

## Working method

- `/sw:workflow` — Shipwright working method for any coding task in a project that has a .quality/project.json file (also by itself)

Also loaded by themselves while Claude builds, never typed: the build rules of each group (`build-design`, `build-security-data`, `build-saas`…) and the rules of the stack modules installed.
